title: mut.channel_mohr_hypercube_projections
mutation_directive: Manfred Mohr — n-dimensional hypercube projections — P-197, P-411 'space.color' series; A Formal Language: 50 Years of Artwork and Algorithms (bitforms 2019). VISUAL SIGNATURE: Sharp geometric line constellations: a 6D, 11D, or higher cube projected into 2D, with lines selectively kept or dropped per algorithmic rules. Reads as exploded crystalline structures, sometimes solid-color filled polygons (the 'space.color' work). Hard-edge, plotter-precise, often saturated primaries on black. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Compute the 2^n vertices of an n-cube (n=6 to 10); pick a random projection matrix from R^n → R^3; render edges as instanced cylinders. Animate by slowly rotating in a randomly-chosen 2-plane of R^n (Givens rotation) — produces hypnotic non-Euclidean tumbling. Per-edge color from a discrete palette (Mohr's primaries: red, blue, yellow, white). No bloom — keep lines crisp. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has no high-dimensional geometry. Strange attractors are 3D dynamical systems; this is pure linear algebra in R^n. Different mathematical lineage entirely. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://www.bitforms.art/exhibition/mohr-2019
